title: Picasso tadpoles with scrambled faces become largely normal frogs

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Picasso tadpoles with scrambled faces become largely normal frogs

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Xenopus tadpoles whose craniofacial organs were placed in abnormal positions ('Picasso tadpoles') tend to become largely normal frogs, because the organs move along novel, abnormal paths and stop at the correct frog-face positions, showing that craniofacial remodelling is goal-directed rather than hardwired.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Goal-Directed Activity in Morphogenesis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Amazingly, they tend to turn into largely normal frogs because the craniofacial organs move in novel, abnormal paths [sometimes overshooting and needing to return a bit (Pinet et al., 2019)] and stop when they get to the correct frog face positions.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Goal-Directed Activity in Morphogenesis”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with experimentally scrambled craniofacial organs undergoing metamorphosis

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Organ motion and final anatomy are measurable from image sequences. Existing reports can test normalization, but stronger trajectory controls are needed to discriminate goal-directed regulation from mechanical developmental alternatives.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Register longitudinal images of scrambled and control tadpoles, quantify organ trajectories and final facial geometry, and test convergence to species-normal positions against passive growth and fixed-trajectory models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Surgery and metamorphic growth create correlated mechanical effects.

Complete longitudinal image series may be unavailable.

Convergence does not uniquely establish goal-directedness.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.88
discriminating power: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.42
data existence: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Endpoint position versus path shape is a direct test, and the Xenopus craniofacial papers report morphometrics for this preparation, including abnormal paths and overshoot. Those measurements are scattered in journal figures rather than an open coordinate file. They can support the setpoint reading for this species and leave mechanical funneling as a live alternative.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track craniofacial organ positions from scrambled tadpole arrangements through metamorphosis and test whether endpoints cluster on the normal frog-face coordinates even when the paths are abnormal or overshoot.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mechanical packing in the head could funnel organs toward the same endpoints.

Landmark time series are published as paper figures and summaries, not as a deposited coordinate table.
